svg.title: Allocate Buyer Capital Before Negotiating Price
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-buyer-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate Buyer Capital Before Negotiating Price; subtitle: Four buckets divide an illustrative $600,000 startup-capital plan.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: The canonical buyer-capital range is $200,000–$1,000,000. The $600,000 illustration allocates 40%, 10%, 30%, and 20%. Boundary allocations use the same illustrative weights, not claims that every transaction is feasible at either boundary.; caption: Numeric values are USD and sum to $600,000. Detail text provides comparable $200,000 and $1,000,000 allocations. Buyer capital is neither recognized sales nor total enterprise value.; stages: label: Purchase equity contribution; value: $240,000; 40% of buyer capital; numeric value: 240000.0; detail: Allocate $80,000 at the lower boundary and $400,000 at the upper boundary. Size debt separately; confirm lender equity requirements and seller-note treatment before treating any note as qualifying injection.; label: Diligence and closing costs; value: $60,000; 10% of buyer capital; numeric value: 60000.0; detail: Allocate $20,000 at the lower boundary and $100,000 at the upper boundary for QoE, counsel, tax work, searches, and transaction expenses. Separate one-time engagement charges from recurring contractor expense.; label: Opening working-capital reserve; value: $180,000; 30% of buyer capital; numeric value: 180000.0; detail: Allocate $60,000 at the lower boundary and $300,000 at the upper boundary. Fund collection gaps and seasonality after reconciling seller-delivered working capital to the negotiated closing adjustment.; label: Integration and contingency liquidity; value: $120,000; 20% of buyer capital; numeric value: 120000.0; detail: Allocate $40,000 at the lower boundary and $200,000 at the upper boundary for migration, retention, and repair contingencies. Cash released for one purpose cannot simultaneously remain available for another.

text.title: Allocate Buyer Capital Before Negotiating Price
text.tspan: Allocate Buyer Capital Before Negotiating Price

rect.title: label: Purchase equity contribution; numeric value: 240000.0; value: $240,000; 40% of buyer capital; detail: Allocate $80,000 at the lower boundary and $400,000 at the upper boundary. Size debt separately; confirm lender equity requirements and seller-note treatment before treating any note as qualifying injection.

text.title: Purchase equity contribution: $240,000; 40% of buyer capital
text.tspan: Purchase equity contribution: $240,000; 40% of buyer capital

rect.title: label: Diligence and closing costs; numeric value: 60000.0; value: $60,000; 10% of buyer capital; detail: Allocate $20,000 at the lower boundary and $100,000 at the upper boundary for QoE, counsel, tax work, searches, and transaction expenses. Separate one-time engagement charges from recurring contractor expense.

text.title: Diligence and closing costs: $60,000; 10% of buyer capital
text.tspan: Diligence and closing costs: $60,000; 10% of buyer capital

rect.title: label: Opening working-capital reserve; numeric value: 180000.0; value: $180,000; 30% of buyer capital; detail: Allocate $60,000 at the lower boundary and $300,000 at the upper boundary. Fund collection gaps and seasonality after reconciling seller-delivered working capital to the negotiated closing adjustment.

Cash released for one purpose cannot simultaneously remain available for another.

text.title: Assumptions: The canonical buyer-capital range is $200,000–$1,000,000. The $600,000 illustration allocates 40%, 10%, 30%, and 20%. Boundary allocations use the same illustrative weights, not claims that every transaction is feasible at either boundary.

Boundary allocations use the same illustrative weights, not claims that every transaction is feasible at either boundary.
